title: Evaluating AI Impact
learning_outcomes: Explain stakeholder impact assessments and how it connects to evaluating ai impact.

content.intro: This lesson covers evaluating ai impact through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Document risk decisions, policy boundaries, stakeholder impact, licensing, applicable law, and governance ownership; legal requirements depend on jurisdiction and use case.
content.why_it_matters: Stakeholder impact assessments requires a documented decision that fits the use case and jurisdiction. Identify affected stakeholders, distinguish binding obligations from voluntary guidance, retain evidence for the decision, and revisit the conclusion when the model, data, product, or applicable rules change.

items.title: Privacy impact assessments
items.text: Privacy impact assessments is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

items.title: Safety and misuse assessments

items.title: Environmental and resource considerations
items.text: Environmental and resource considerations supports a repeatable development workflow. Keep dependencies and model choices explicit, preserve small input/output fixtures, isolate credentials from source code, and document how another learner can reproduce the result on a compatible environment.

items.title: Monitoring unintended impacts after deployment
items.text: Use monitoring unintended impacts after deployment to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice stakeholder impact assessments within evaluating ai impact: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.

summary: Evaluating AI Impact is one part of a larger generative AI application lifecycle.
Use explicit inputs, criteria, and reproducible examples to test the concept.
Document uncertainty, failure modes, security considerations, and version assumptions.
